md_cover_card.notesMarkdown:
Use Cover for ordinary blinds. Doors, garages and gates belong to Access, whose opening control requires a deliberate slide.

Position, open, close and stop controls follow supported_features and current_position. Confirmed reports glide over 200–500 ms; target changes remain immediate. Sparse reports pause at the last confirmed position. Reduced motion snaps to the report.

The name sits above the position bar, top-aligned with the icon on its right. Longer names wrap naturally. The bold current state floats against the left edge of the position bar while it fits before the target thumb, then moves to the right edge when the left side is too narrow. If neither side fits the full label, it wraps in the roomier space. Covers without position support keep the state below the name.

md_climate_card.notesMarkdown:
Measured temperature, actual activity and availability remain authoritative. Requested mode/targets can show pending feedback until HA confirms or rejects them.

Climate uses a compact readings-first layout: a large unitless current temperature, reported activity and an optional humidity reading beside the vertical target selector. The normal scalar selector has 8px above and below it; long names, ranges, graphs and enlarged text grow naturally.

Choose **Humidity sensor** to show that sensor's reported percentage on the card and in details. Missing or invalid readings show a neutral dash without disabling the thermostat. Clearing the selection hides humidity.

**Enable climate popup** defaults to enabled. Details show readings first, supported modes next, and the same target selector at the lower right. Disabling it exposes supported modes inline unless **Mode buttons** is explicitly false. Mode choices use named 48px icon buttons and a localized selected-mode heading; narrow layouts wrap them. Custom actions, popup references and authored layouts remain saved when the popup is disabled.

variables.humidity_entity.description: Optional reported humidity; unset/null/empty hides the reading.

variables.enable_popup.description: Enable built-in details. False retains targets and exposes inline modes.

variables.show_mode_buttons.description: Show inline modes when the popup is disabled; details retain supported choices.

humidity.label: Humidity
humidity.description: Show the selected sensor on the card and in details.

inline-modes.label: Inline modes
inline-modes.description: Disable built-in details and show supported choices on the card.

md_media_card.notesMarkdown:
Popup is the default. Inline places the same owned media controls on the dashboard.

Playback, seek, volume, sources and remote controls depend on the entity’s capabilities; selection lists use the reported sources. Built-in media and Apple TV remote buttons use a single tap, including directions and Select. They show brief press feedback without a hold countdown or long command.

## Plex library

See the dedicated [Plex library](../plex-library/) page for setup, Plex and Rivulet configuration, TV selection and real-card gallery examples. Enable it through this Media card’s **Apple TV options → Plex setup**.

md_glance_card.notesMarkdown:
Each reading has its own rounded tile, with a circular icon above the value and wrapping name. Three tiles fit across a normal full-width phone layout with 8px gaps; fewer readings fill the available width. Narrower hosts or enlarged text reflow to fewer columns. Healthy tiles stay readable during partial availability.

Tap an Activity icon to inspect recorded events with date and type filters. Optional variables.activity_entities adds explicitly related sources. Automatic Updated and last-activation timestamps move into Activity; timestamp-sensor readings remain data.

Turn off **Show reading labels** in the card editor to show only icons and values. In YAML, set `variables.show_reading_names: false`. Labels remain visible by default; the group title has its own visibility setting. Custom reading names are retained when hidden and return when labels are enabled again. Activity buttons keep their entity names for accessibility.

Each of the three optional readings has an independent entity, name and icon. One unavailable reading does not erase the other values.

variables.show_reading_names.description: Show or hide all reading labels without changing the group title or saved names.

navbar.notesMarkdown:
Ordinary dashboards configure navigation once in the top-level marao.navbar block. The standalone card shown here exposes the same runtime for the demonstration; do not add one per view.

Choose **Marao settings → Current room → This browser → Area sensor for this browser** to follow a sensor directly without a person. Different browsers/devices sharing one HA account can select different sensors. The choice is browser-local, separate from the YAML below; see [navigation setup](../../features/navigation/) for persistence and reset behavior. Existing person mappings and Automatic remain available as explicitly labelled legacy tracking.

Bermuda room resolution uses the configured area sensor’s area_id. It does not infer rooms from display names or last_seen.

A missing, unknown, unmapped or unavailable room retains a disabled away-style slot so navigation does not move. Only legacy person tracking uses presence and the optional configured Away page; direct sensor mode stays neutral when its own reading is missing.

All configured entries remain reachable. A rightmost More control opens vertical overflow when the row is full.

An invisible touch barrier covers the full screen width from the navbar's top edge to the bottom. Only navbar controls respond in that strip; cards behind it cannot be tapped or scrolled. Open popups remain interactive above it.

default.label: Current room
default.description: Legacy preview: Alex is home in the Living room.

away.label: Away page
away.description: Legacy person tracking uses Away even if its room sensor is stale.

md_schedules_card.notesMarkdown:
An administrator sets up the collection and acknowledges dedicated devices. Home Assistant owns its automations; the browser does not need to stay open. Keep native Home Assistant backups before resource changes.

Groups are collapsible sections with only one open at a time. The active group opens initially; its switch activates or pauses it. Opening a section does not activate it. Pausing or switching groups does not cancel accepted timed runs. Use the labelled group-add control below the divider.

Timer rows show essential settings and an enable switch. Tap a timer to edit its name, local time, on/off action and weekdays in the popup. New timers use the card-configured devices and their parent section. Add a separate off timer rather than a duration; existing duration-based records retain their saved behavior.

Edits save automatically and errors remain visible. Closing with the top-right close button flushes pending changes; the red trash action deletes the timer. Weekdays use a themed multi-select dropdown. Add a timer with the left-aligned plus; Delete group appears beneath it on the right.

Configuration reloads and automation state changes refresh automatically. The card has no manual Refresh, Delete collection, device-status list, recovery export, duration editor or per-timer group/device picker. Structural external edits and ambiguous ownership remain read-only until reconciled.

md_weather_card.notesMarkdown: The static sky reflects the reported weather condition; no background is animated. A large whole-number temperature appears with available wind, humidity and pressure readings. Metrics wrap naturally without empty slots; displayed current and forecast values are rounded without changing reported data. Tap the card to open hourly predictions or up to seven days on matching condition scenery, according to the entity’s capabilities. Explicit custom tap and hold actions retain their configured behavior. Missing forecasts stay empty and reported errors remain visible. `variables.show_forecast: false` hides the forecast entry.

plex-library.notesMarkdown:
## Library layout

Choose **Library layout** in **Apple TV options → Plex setup**. **On dashboard** shows the complete library; **Popup** shows the compact poster card and opens all three shelves in a Marao popup. The compact card contains the TV name, library title, a content reference and poster artwork, with no bottom counters. Choose **On dashboard** for the parent Media card’s controls when placing it directly on your dashboard. Existing Plex configurations without this option keep full shelves.

The saved option is `apple_tv.plex.display: inline` or `popup`. Shelf request and artwork errors stay inside the affected shelf, each with its own Retry; a failed library request gives each of the three shelves its own error without coloring the entire library red.

## Setup and playback

Open this card's **Apple TV options → Plex setup** to enable the owned Plex Watch section. It uses this card's television automatically. Choose **Plex** or **Rivulet** as the **Playback app** here rather than creating another TV card. With several configured Apple TV cards, the library's Marao dropdown lets you switch between their named mappings. Opening from a different Apple TV card selects that card's TV again.

Add Home Assistant's **Plex Media Server** integration first. Use the same single Plex server/profile in HA and the selected Apple TV app. For **Plex** playback, open Plex on the TV once so HA can discover its media-player client. Select that **Plex client**, the integration's **Scan-clients button**, and the exact **Plex app source** supported by this card's TV. **Choose library folders** browses HA's returned servers; choose **Use this server**. If Continue Watching discovery is ambiguous, open the appropriate recommendation folder and select **Use for Continue Watching**. Setup and browsing do not wake a television or change server settings.

The library home has exactly three open shelves: **Continue Watching**, **Movies**, and **TV Series**, in that order. Each shelf scrolls independently with native horizontal touch scrolling and visible Previous/Next controls. Larger portrait covers (about 160 × 240px) have wrapping titles below them; **Load more** extends that rail without resetting the others. Movie/show shelves merge first-level contents of matching libraries in returned order, using media metadata rather than library names; identical references are deduplicated, while distinct editions remain. Unclassified libraries are checked by their direct children, and failures stay readable alongside usable shelves. No seasons or per-title metadata are fetched until browsing. Tap an episode or movie to resume/play; show and season tiles open their contents. Opening a series from the dashboard keeps the home shelves in place; details inside a media sheet reuse that sheet. Back restores shelf positions and retains the selected TV. **Browse library** offers the library tree and Recently Added when supplied by Plex. Missing recommendations and empty folders have separate explanations; unavailable artwork uses a neutral poster. Only metadata supplied by HA is shown, so the card does not invent watch-progress percentages. **Refresh** and **Retry** are explicit actions; the library does not poll in the background.

One title tap gives strong haptic feedback and wakes an off TV. **Plex** playback opens Plex and waits up to 30 seconds for its mapped Plex client before sending one playback request. **Rivulet** playback sends a movie/episode link directly to the selected Apple TV; Rivulet opens and resumes at its saved position. It requires Rivulet with content-link support (confirmed in v1.2.0-122), already signed into the same selected Plex server/profile. The link does not switch servers/profiles. No Plex app launch or client scan is needed for Rivulet playback. Already-satisfied steps are skipped. Changing TV, closing the browser, editing the card or losing the connection cancels subsequent launch steps. Requests already sent to HA cannot be recalled. A readable failure allows an explicit retry; the existing Now playing display remains based on HA reports.

The Watch section is available in automatic **Popup** and **On dashboard** media presentations. In a popup, library navigation stays in that sheet; inline cards open Marao's normal library sheet. Explicit custom popup layouts remain independently authored: switch deliberately to automatic details before enabling this section. Ordinary app shortcuts keep their existing source-launch action.

For **Rivulet**, choose your configured server using **Choose library folders → Use this server**. HA 2026.10 exposes Plex browsing through a registered media-player entity, including inactive session entities. Play something once in Rivulet so HA can discover a session; then use **Retry** in the card. The card automatically finds an enabled Plex entity for that server, or you can choose a **Plex browse entity (optional)**. That entity supplies library/Continue Watching metadata and never receives Rivulet playback commands. Until discovery, the card shows a setup explanation and retains your real server selection. The official Plex app is not required for Rivulet playback.

The optional configuration lives under `apple_tv.plex`; use the visual folder picker for the returned content references:

```yaml
type: custom:marao-media-card
entity_id: media_player.example_apple_tv
apple_tv:
  remote_entity: remote.example_apple_tv
  plex:
    client_entity: media_player.example_plex_client
    scan_clients_entity: button.example_plex_scan_clients
    app_source: Plex
    library_root:
      media_content_type: server
      media_content_id: plex://example-server/server
```

For Rivulet, replace the playback-only client/scan/source fields with `playback_app: rivulet` and keep the selected server reference:

```yaml
apple_tv:
  remote_entity: remote.example_apple_tv
  plex:
    playback_app: rivulet
    # Optional: any registered Plex entity belonging to this server.
    # browse_entity: media_player.example_plex_session
    library_root:
      media_content_type: server
      media_content_id: plex://example-server/server
```

These IDs are fictional. Missing `playback_app` retains Plex playback. Missing `plex` or `plex: false` keeps the section disabled; an optional `continue_watching` object uses the same `media_content_type`/`media_content_id` shape. No Plex password or token belongs in this configuration. Credentials and poster authentication stay with HA through its Plex image proxy. This feature does not switch Plex profiles, manage the server/library, edit watch history, manage queues or stream via AirPlay.
